title: What exactly is Fascism?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss fascism: its origins with Benito Mussolini and the term's roots in the Latin fasces, its contrast with democracy and communism, its emphasis on war, Darwinian survival of the fittest, and authoritarian cults of personality. They cover how fascists exploited post-World War I crisis, the Treaty of Versailles, idealized pasts, and ethnic scapegoating, plus the difference between Mussolini's and Hitler's versions, treatment of women, youth, gays, and religion. They note fascist states in Germany, Italy, Romania, and Franco's Spain, why the movement faded after World War II, neo-fascist offshoots, and a closing listener mail segment about Boba Fett and the Wilhelm scream.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction
segments.summary: Hosts open the episode with banter about being called fascists and announce the topic of fascism, with Mussolini's role in creating the term introduced.

segments.title: Mussolini, the word fascism, and its misuse
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss Mussolini coining the term fascism, its drawing on ancient Roman military techniques, and the word being widely misused in everyday political talk.

segments.title: Etymology: fasces
segments.summary: The word is traced to the Italian fascio and Latin fasces, a bundle of sticks tied around an axe, which the hosts use as a metaphor for the state and the people.

segments.title: Fascism versus democracy and communism
segments.summary: The hosts describe fascism as the opposite of democracy with the state above the individual, distinguish it from communism, and note its rigid social classes.

segments.title: War, Darwinism, and imperialism
segments.summary: Fascism is described as centered on waging and winning war, justified by Darwinian survival of the fittest, with Mussolini's quote about war ennobling people.

segments.title: How fascists gained public support
segments.summary: The hosts explain that fascists exploited nations in crisis, such as Germany after World War I and the Treaty of Versailles, offering a return to a mythical past and scapegoating one ethnic group.

segments.title: Mussolini's versus Hitler's fascism
segments.summary: The hosts contrast capital F Fascism of Mussolini, focused on war for glory, with Hitler's conquest aimed at furthering the Aryan race, and quote Giovanni Gentile on progress through division.

segments.title: Authoritarianism, violence, and life under fascism
segments.summary: The hosts discuss cults of personality, domestic violence against dissenters, the Final Solution, the treatment of women, youth, and gay people, and rallies and religion under fascist states.

segments.title: Fascist states, decline, and neo-fascism
segments.summary: Fascist states in Germany, Italy, Romania, and Spain under Franco are named; the movement faded after World War II; neo-fascist groups such as love of difference and their violent acts are mentioned, along with markers of fascist policy.
topics: decline of fascism after World War II

segments.title: Wrap-up and listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts close with a pointer to further reading and read listener mail about Boba Fett and the Wilhelm scream, then sign off.
